cases.description: new_intent/match on a clean slate (no active process_id) -> sap_form_filling, the single-entry processes list spread onto the result

new_intent/match while a process is already active -> still sap_form_filling directly; parking an active process before a new one starts is Intent Manager's unconditional pre-Router job now, not this node's concern

REGRESSION: new_intent/match while a process is already active with real in-progress form_state -> the active process's form_state survives untouched, even though Agent: Find's own new_intent output contract includes a literal form_state: null -- Intent Manager (running right after this file) needs the real value intact to snapshot into the paused node when it parks it; a live test caught this actually wiping a user's in-progress purchase request the moment they asked an unrelated question

REGRESSION: new_intent/match with a real user message -> the real message survives untouched, even though Agent: Find's own new_intent/match output contract includes a literal message: null -- a live test traced this to the exact cause of every downstream node (Agent: Form's chatInput, in particular) seeing the user's message as null on a fresh match/batch classification

cases.description: pending_reply against a genuinely active node -> sap_form_filling (pending_kind removed entirely 2026-08-13 -- status: pending_reply only ever meant form_fill once selection/batch_confirm/stack_resume were removed, so this no longer branches on pending_kind at all)

REGRESSION: pending_reply against a node that's already completed (a stale/misclassified continuation -- Agent: Find is an LLM, not a guaranteed-correct state read) -> does NOT route to sap_form_filling; this is the actual fix for the crash a stale active_node_id used to cause deep inside SAP execution (Build Execution Prompt, GET_QUERY on a process_definition pruned to just {name}) -- caught here instead, at the decision to route at all. Resumes active_node_id to the nearest open ancestor and reactivates it.
pending_reply with no active_node_id/intention_nodes at all -> not a valid continuation target, resumes to null, no crash
new_intent/batch on a clean slate -> batch_processing, the multi-entry processes list spread onto the result
new_intent/batch while a process is already active -> still batch_processing directly, same reasoning as the match case above
new_intent/no_match -> classified for delivery within this same file (route_key stays null; Intent Manager is never involved), with the agent's own composed message
new_intent/error -> classified for delivery within this same file, route_key stays null
unparseable agent output (_parse_error true) -> flagged as a PARSE_ERROR rather than silently routing nowhere, route_key stays null
